Two corrections and one new capability.

**The agreement report overstated double-rating.** `scripts/iaa_report.py` counted
judgment *rows* per pair, so a pair the same annotator judged twice counted as two
independent opinions. It printed 174 "multi-annotated" pairs where Krippendorff's alpha,
the corpus release trigger and the Admin panel all said 107 — and 107 was right. On the
current corpus, 174 of 1,120 judgments are the same person re-judging a pair they had
already judged.

Alpha itself was never affected; it has always been computed on one score per
(pair, annotator). But the raw and binarized agreement figures in that report were
inflated by annotators trivially agreeing with themselves: raw exact agreement falls
from 0.7529 to 0.7290, and binarized agreement from 0.9494 to 0.9286. Anyone quoting the
earlier numbers should use these.

**Admin edits were being written to a local snapshot.** The panel's default data source
is a copy pulled from the server, so the gloss accept/reject buttons changed nothing in
production and every decision was discarded by the next refresh, silently. Curation now
goes to the live server first and is mirrored locally only if that succeeds.

**Gloss review and corpus cleaning are now one pass.** The queue is a batch form with
three outcomes per item — keep the gloss, discard the gloss, or withdraw the row as not
a saying. Withdrawal records who did it, when and why, and is reversible from a panel
directly below. Nothing is ever deleted: a withdrawn row stays in the database and in
the provenance record, it simply stops being served, counted, clustered or mapped.
